original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: In F2[GL(3,F2)], with paid labels exactly the 21 matrices g satisfying rank(g+I)=1 and with rank-one idempotent scalar mixing on all W registers, every diagonal endpoint diag([g1],...,[gW]) has exact call length sum rank(gi+I). The named width-3 endpoint diag([T1],[R2],[S]) has length 6.
scope_change_reason: The card permits one specified nonabelian operation family. The family is the 21 defining-representation transvections of GL(3,F2), not the additive group of M3(Q) and not the six coordinate generators I+Eij. Endpoints are diagonal, at every finite width, with the width-3 word above as the explicit identity.
bottleneck_link: The complex primitive binds the selected construction, so a finite GL(3,F2) identity cannot move kappa by itself. The bit-mechanism question is whether this nonabelian alphabet undercuts the nine-call shape of the three-register obstruction. Three order-7 elements still cost exactly 9, and every diagonal bill equals the defining-rank sum.
stop_rule: Stop after the diagonal tariff for this 21-label alphabet. Do not search non-diagonal endpoints or reopen the six-label coordinate census.
evidence: Uniform representation-rank lower bound plus an exhaustive transvection factorization of all 168 group elements. Verifier: PASS_GL3_TRANSVECTION_DIAGONAL_FLOOR elements=168 transvections=21 witness_calls=6 target_rank=6 coordinate_length_S=4 coordinate_length_3cycle=6 width2_pairs=28224 controls=8 no_new_kappa.

open_questions.question: Is there an explicit non-diagonal endpoint in M2(F2[GL(3,F2)]), in this same 21-label alphabet, whose exact minimum exceeds the rank of its defining-representation image?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The diagonal theorem is sharp because represented rank equals the direct bill. A gap would mean the relaxation stops being a tariff once off-diagonal group-algebra entries are allowed.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate all 588 calls on two registers and all 588^2 ordered pairs. Keep an endpoint that equals no shorter call and whose 6 by 6 image has rank below 2.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing mathematical blocks that finite screen. It was not run in this package. Words longer than two calls are a separate search.
